title: The first house on Douglas Avenue
deck: What a $62,000 rental in Wichita taught me about the part of business nobody puts in the spreadsheet.
text: The closing took eleven minutes. I had read for eight months on BiggerPockets about cash flow, cap rates and the one percent rule, and the whole thing came down to a woman in a title office sliding papers across a desk while a space heater ticked in the corner. Then I owned a house on Douglas Avenue and a tenant I had never met. The spreadsheet said the house would clear two hundred and ten dollars a month. The spreadsheet did not say that the tenant's son would call me at 9:40 on a Tuesday night because the furnace had quit, or that I would spend the next hour on the phone finding someone to come look at it, or that I would lie awake afterward wondering whether I was the kind of person who could do this. I was not, yet. Every owner I have talked to since has a version of that night. The numbers are the easy part. The work is the phone calls nobody else wants to make, and whether you make them. That is what this site is about.
